doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Big B-A-D Band personnel
summary: Saxes, trombones, trumpets and rhythm players who passed through the band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, I wrote some things, and Bob wrote some things, Holloway wrote some things – Roger Kellaway, rather, wrote some things. Everybody contributed something.
Who were some of the other personnel of that aggregation, besides Chris Woods?

The Big B-A-D Band. Oh, I didn’t write anything for the Big B-A-D Band. I’m talking about the combo, I wrote. No, I wasn’t too much into big-band writing. In the big band, Ernie Wilkins, who wrote for us. He played tenor [saxophone]. We had Charles Davis on baritone [saxophone]. We had Charlie Williams on alto [saxophone], Chris Woods.

C. I. Williams, yeah. Let’s see. I’m trying to think of who else. Trombones were John Gordon and Jimmy Wilkins, Ernie’s brother, and a cat from Quinnipiac College, Sonny Costanzo. In the trumpets we had – we had a couple of different trumpet sections. One was Lloyd Michaels, Johnny Melita – what’s his name – Gamby. Oscar Gamby. I’m naming all the trumpet players that I can think of that were in there.
Ray Copeland. Yeah, Ray played the Carnegie Hall concert with us.
Ernie – Ernie Royal play with that?
Ernie Royal started out with us, but he didn’t – he always put us out, because he was so busy. He’d say, “I think this band should disband.” Yeah, Copeland was one of our mainstays.

I was just going to say Lew Soloff. Let’s see. Who else was in there? A little cat that ended up in the Basie band. He was my manager’s son, Carley – Dale Carley, a great little player. We had Victor Sproles on bass. Don Friedman was there for a while, and – I can see these cats. I can’t call all their names right now.
Did Ron Carter play in that band?

Ron Carter was the very first, when we had Ernie Wilkins and Ron Carter. Ron was the beginning, and of course Patti Bown was the original piano player. We had Grady Tate for a while. Big Eddie Jones on bass. I don’t know. We had so many cats in there.
